text:
Is Salary Jump A New ‘Burden’ For Middle Class? Rs 75 Lakh Job Offer Sparks Tax Debate
The man expressed his hesitation about accepting the new role, not because of the work, but because of the significant increase in tax liability.
Who doesn’t like a salary hike? A higher salary can improve financial security, allow for better planning for the future, and provide a greater sense of financial well-being, right? But it looks like it’s not a similar case in India, as for many residents here, it might be a ‘burden’, even if it is a Rs 75 Lakh job offer, and the reason- High Income Tax.
What happened?
Recommended Stories
Taking to Reddit, a user shared his confusion about whether he should accept a new Rs 75 Lakh p.a. job offer, a significant rise from his current Rs 48 Lakh p.a. package, or not. He expressed his hesitation about accepting the new role, not because of the work, but because of the significant increase in tax liability that comes with the greater compensation.
Further explaining his confusion, he remarked, “At present, I pay around Rs 12 lakhs in taxes. With the new offer, that figure nearly doubles to Rs 22 lakhs, especially because of the additional 10 percent surcharge applicable on income above Rs 50 lakhs."
This shows that, while the gross income increase appears to be significant, the effective increase in in-hand pay is only about 50 percent after tax deduction.
Why should I pay more tax?
He went on to say that the new remuneration structure lacks the flexibility to integrate tax-saving components. “So, while my take-home earnings may rise by around 50 percent, my tax burden nearly doubles. It poses a fundamental question for me: why should I work much harder merely to pay more to the government, when others who pay little or no tax receive no further tangible benefits?" he asked.
How did social media react?
The post sparked a debate on social media, with several users empathising with his situation. A Reddit user commented, “Unfortunately, it is how it works when you’re in the higher brackets, especially as a salaried person. If possible, maybe you can negotiate them to not be employed but paid as a consultant, then you’d be able to save a big amount but not taking a pay raise because you don’t want to pay higher to the government is just hurting yourself to hurt someone that doesn’t even feel the pinch."
Another one shared, “The right thing will be to forget that you pay taxes, and take up the role. It’ll help you take larger packages in your next job jump. As long as you are in India, at large, take it as a norm and accept that the government will syphon off more and more taxes to distribute goodies, buy votes and build absurd bridges."
A person wrote, “Accept the damn offer. You’ll be saving good despite the increased tax. Even if you don’t save at all." Another comment read, “I feel you by every word and every character in every word. I have spent years burning my brain on this, rant about it, be frustrated about it, and cursing it etc., but what does it do? Nothing."
Income Tax in India:
The tax slab rates for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27) are: Income up to Rs 4 lakh is exempt, followed by Rs 4 lakh – Rs 8 lakh at 5 percent, Rs.8 lakh – Rs.12 lakh at 10 percent, Rs 12 lakh – Rs 16 lakh at 15 percent, Rs 16 lakh – Rs.20 lakh at 20 percent, Rs 20 lakh – Rs 24 lakh at 25 percent, and income beyond Rs 24 lakh at 30 percent.
